Information since September points to a strong labor market and moderate growth, but the noted weakness in business fixed investment is meaningful: investment-led fluctuations are central to business cycles and can account for sizable swings in real GDP (investment function/accelerator; Gomme; Christiano–Eichenbaum). With both headline and core inflation running below 2 percent and market-based inflation compensation low, New Keynesian evidence on inflation dynamics (Galí, Gertler, and López-Salido) and rules-based analyses (Taylor; McCallum and Nelson, 1999) support a modest easing bias to stabilize the output gap and re-anchor expectations. The Fed’s decision to cut the funds rate to 1.50–1.75% and to use Treasury bill purchases and repo operations to maintain ample reserves is consistent with the literature documenting monetary policy’s real effects when transmission through money markets is smooth (B. Friedman; St. Louis tradition; Sims, 1992). Overall tone: cautiously dovish—supportive of continued expansion but attentive to downside risks from soft investment/exports and muted inflation pressures.
